content.text: All children ≥2yrs: BMI calculated at least annually to determine percentile

•BMI = funct of wt & height (considers sex) - convenient measure of body fat % - children: BMI percentile for age & sex (adults: absolute #) - thresholds become adult values as kids approach adulthood

•slowing height velocity by 3–5y → childhood short stature
•growth spurt & puberty eventually occur - final adult height norm
•transient defect in hypothalamic GnRH prod ← physio individual variation - MCC of 2° hypogonadism
: ⍉2° sex characteristics @ age when 95% of same sex & culture have started maturation - US ≈12y girls · ≈14y boys
•Eti: 1° hypogonadism (Klinefelter · Turner) · 2° hypogonadism (constitutional delay MC · isolated GnRH deficiency) · GH deficiency · hyperprolactinemia · hypothyroidism
•isolated GnRH deficiency: male infants → micropenis & cryptorchidism
•congenital: may ⍉be noticed @ birth - abnorm postnatal growth in 1st few mo/yrs → delayed bone age · height velocity slows & deviates from expected curve
•acquired: growth failure · delayed bone age · ↑wt:height ratio - Eti: pituitary tumor (MC) · hypothalamic tumor · head trauma · radiation to head
•children: growth failure · short stature · hypoglycemia · prolonged conj hyperbilirubinemia - adults: ↓lean body mass · ↑fat mass · ↓energy · ↓BMD
Short stature: height >2 SD below avg for sex & age (= 2.3rd percentile)
•MC nonpathologic Eti: familial short stature · constitutional delay of growth & puberty
•pathologic: Turner · IBD · malabsorb · malnutrition · hormonal abnorm
•↓height velocity (growing slower than expected - relative plateau on curve) merits eval for 2° Eti even w.o short stature
Norm growth velocity: birth–12mo 24cm/yr · 12–24mo 10cm/yr · 2–3y 8cm/yr · 4–6y 5–8.5cm/yr · 6y–puberty: boys 4–6cm/yr · girls 4.5–6.5cm/yr · puberty 8–14cm/yr (15% of adult height)

- IUGR · placental dysfun · intrauterine infect · teratogens · trisomy 21 · Turner’s syndrome
- malnutrition · chronic systemic dz · psychosocial deprivation · drugs · hypothyroidism · GH deficiency · glucocorticoid excess · precocious puberty
Bone age (AP XR of Lt wrist)
•initial eval: growth chart · height velocity · parents' heights (projected growth) - endo screening labs PRN
•↓height velocity → bone age (hand & wrist XR) - if bone age >2 SD from mean → recalculate projected height from bone age
•cortisol: if Cushing sxs (obesity · atrophic skin · purple striae · early puberty) - ↑wt for height USU → hypothyroidism (TSH)
•tTG (celiac → malnutrition · malabsorb · short stature) ⍉USU 1st test for ↓growth
•eval if height for age deviates across 2 major percentile curves - 2–4y: height velocity <5.5cm/yr = growth failure → test thyroid · chronic systemic dz · malabsorb · skeletal dx
•↓IGF-1 & IGFBP-3 + delayed bone age → GH stim test to confirm GH deficiency (agents: clonidine · arginine · glucagon)
•brain MRI (hypothalamic-pituitary stalk) after clin & biochem dx of GH deficiency - r/o tumor
→ hypothalamic or pituitary process resulting in ↓GH secretion from the pituitary
Pubertal delay wrkup: Lt hand & wrist XR (bone age < chronological age) · growth chart · CBC · kidney panel · ESR · LFTs · IgA anti-tTG (celiac) · LH · FSH · testosterone (boys) · estradiol (girls)
•finds underlying Eti: IBD · anorexia nervosa · hepatic dz · celiac
Constitutional delay: reassurance + repeat eval in 3–6mo (resolves spont)
2° hypogonadism w few/⍉signs of puberty: short-term testosterone (boys >14y) · estradiol (girls >12y) - ⍉LH/FSH
tx underlying cause (IBD · celiac → gluten-free diet)
GH deficiency: GH replace - dietary chgs ⍉help (growth failure ⍉← poor intake)
MC ← CYP21A2 gene mut - autosomal recessive → 21-hydroxylase deficiency (MC · >95%)
Classic form: insuff cortisol synth · mineralocorticoid deficiency · ↑androgens
US: all newborns screened - undiagnosed & untx → adrenal crisis
Genital atypia common: labial fusion · urogenital sinus · clitoral enlrg → examine thoroughly for CAH
Adrenal crisis: vomiting · diarrhea · hypotension · unexplained fever
•testosterone levels may be monitored for hyperandrogenism (⍉tx in neonates)
•hydrocortisone = steroid of choice - prednisone + hydrocortisone together unnecessary
⍉dexamethasone + fludrocortisone combo: overtreatment risk (dexamethasone longer-acting · more potent) · suboptimal adult height · lacks NaCl
CAH found prenatally: dexamethasone during preg
